content.text:
Six of the eight steps are done and committed on branch `t3/self-hosted`. The full browser test suite (85 tests) is still running, and I'll pick it up again when it finishes.

**What works now:**
1. **Backend in Docker.** `npm run setup` writes fresh secrets to `.env`, starts Postgres plus the Supabase pieces on `127.0.0.1` only, applies all 105 migrations and creates the owner account. Running it again is safe.
2. **No login screen.** Moneo signs you in automatically. Sign-out, password reset and "Delete account" are removed.
3. **Background jobs without Vercel.** The server runs summaries, review recovery, bank sync and Scalable sync a minute after start and then hourly. Each sync still runs about once a day. All four returned success against the real backend.
4. **Scalable Capital works unchanged.** I tested the connect step live and Scalable returned its login link. Finishing it needs your Scalable login and 2FA.
5. **AI access in Settings, with two equal options:** "Sign in with ChatGPT" and an OpenAI API key, and you choose which one pays. I followed OpenAI's guide for open-source local apps. Voice calls and dictation still need the API key, because ChatGPT plan usage doesn't support audio.
6. **Docs:** README, AGENTS.md, and a BACKLOG entry for phone access.

**Changes from what we discussed:**
- **Own compose file instead of the Supabase CLI.** The CLI exposes the database to your whole network using publicly known default passwords, so I wrote a compose file that binds to `127.0.0.1` only.
- **Next.js bound to `127.0.0.1`.** It listened on every network interface by default, which combined with automatic sign-in would have exposed your finances to anyone on your Wi-Fi.

**Not verified yet:**
- **ChatGPT sign-in.** The button reaches OpenAI's sign-in page, but Cloudflare's bot check stops an automated browser there, and the unit tests use mocked OpenAI replies. Please try one real sign-in in Settings → AI access.
- **Browser tests.** Two failures so far. One tested the removed sign-in pages, and I deleted that test. The other two (a Settings "Preferences saved" message and an account check on Home/Plan) I'll look into once the run finishes.

**Things you need to know:**
- **Bank sync with real banks won't work yet.** Enable Banking production apps only accept `https://` return addresses, so `http://localhost` is rejected. Sandbox (mock banks) works. I've put options in BACKLOG; the simplest is a small static HTTPS page that forwards the bank's reply back to your localhost.
- **Your old hosted settings are backed up** to `.env.cloud.bak` (gitignored). The new `.env` keeps your OpenAI and Enable Banking keys.
- **Still to do:** remove the hosted Privacy and Terms pages, then run the full unit tests, lint and build. Nothing has been pushed or opened as a PR.

- [OpenAI: Models and inference](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference)

-    <main className="flex min-h-screen justify-center bg-background px-5 py-12">

-
-            Moneo is not launched yet and is still being built. This notice describes the current plan and will be updated before launch.

-

Moneo is a personal-finance workspace for understanding your money, planning decisions, and building reusable tools with AI. You add data with CSV/Excel imports, manual entries, or a read-only bank connection.

-

Your email for sign-in, and any financial data you import or enter: accounts, transactions, balances, goals, budgets, AI conversations, and voice calls with Moneo. If you connect a bank, also the balances and booked transactions it shares.

-

How your data is used

-

Only to run your private workspace: show balances and forecasts, run calculations from application code, and answer your AI questions. Financial calculations come from application code, not AI guesses.

-

AI and third parties

-

When you use AI features, the context needed to answer is sent to the model provider (OpenAI or OpenRouter, depending on the model you choose); voice calls send your audio to OpenAI. Mapping an import can send its column headers and up to eight sample rows. Settings controls what AI can read. Your workspace is stored with our hosting and database providers (Vercel and Supabase). Bank connections run through Enable Banking with your consent. They bring data in only and never move money, and you can disconnect them in Settings.

-

What we do not do

-

No selling your data, no advertising use, no public sharing of your workspace. Original records are preserved with history and undo.

-

Keeping and deleting your data

-

Your data is kept until you remove it. Reset all data empties your workspace and keeps your account. Delete account permanently removes your account, your workspace, your uploaded files and your bank connections. Both are in Settings.

-

For a question about your data, or if you can no longer sign in and want your account deleted, email mgsukhan@gmail.com.

-

e2e/README.md:7:The gate checks chosen question/focus/dates/planning through UI dispatch and reload, material decline drill-down, retained checkpoint-response loss and durable retry, support exhaustion, unavailable follow-ups, an actual read deadline with zero synthesis transport calls, source fingerprint change with unchanged historical output, and Stop settling the actual synthesis fetch before suppressing publication. Exact fixture IDs are deleted in `finally`; Next runs in `.qa/mne019-runtime`, and the harness stops its Windows Next process tree on shutdown. Run only with the shared heavy/browser slot released, ports3040/3041 free, and Playwright Chromium installed. These prepared tests require execution; syntax/lint checks are not runtime acceptance. Real SQL ownership/reservation races, Supabase authentication and deployed acceptance remain separate gates.
e2e/README.md:15:Daily scheduling is compatible with Vercel Hobby. For up to 25 eligible jobs and healthy services, deadline convergence occurs at the next daily invocation (about 24 hours plus the cadence and platform scheduling delay); a backlog takes further invocations. Persistent service failures are reported and cannot guarantee a wall-clock bound. Actual deployed cron registration, credentials, invocations and Vercel durable-queue behavior require separate deployment acceptance; local runtime/SQL tests do not establish them.
e2e/README.md:21:`e2e/provider-stop.gated.spec.ts` requires deployed migration 202610060013 and real disposable Supabase authentication. It checks owned Stop/reload requested versus acknowledged state, an explicitly unconfirmed termination receipt, late-publication suppression, completed report retention and unchanged intentional correction/history. Its worker acknowledgment is a controlled service receipt; the separate installed-runtime HTTP test establishes real transport abort. Recovery allows a canceled runtime's running step time to acknowledge, then uses `cancellation_unconfirmed` for stale steps rather than claiming termination. Runtime/step lookup failures remain recoverable, and missing cancellation timestamps use the existing 24-hour deadline. Actual hosted Workflow/provider cancellation remains a separate deployment check.
e2e/README.md:25:The required tier fails on absent prerequisites, failed commands, empty reports, any unit/browser skip, or flaky browser results. It also requires the latest fast result to pass on a clean checkout and match the current commit and `.next/BUILD_ID`; rerun `npm run acceptance:fast` after any commit, uncommitted change or replacement build. Configure `.env` with `SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`; supply `E2E_STORAGE_STATE` (or `e2e/.auth.json`) for an empty disposable synthetic workspace. Install Playwright Chromium and apply the repository migration head through your normal reviewed deployment process before browser acceptance. Stop any existing port3000 server before the fast build; stop any port3000 server before the required tier too: it starts the verified production build with `npm start`, without HMR, existing-server reuse or a live provider key. `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1` selects that production server for direct Playwright runs; ordinary runs retain the development server.
e2e/README.md:31:Actual provider quality/cancellation evaluation is a separate optional, explicitly budgeted tier, not run by either command. The existing `core-journey.gated.spec.ts` invokes the live provider and is explicitly excluded from the required tier and recorded in its summary; run that journey separately when provider evaluation is authorized. Browser AI mocks remain deterministic contracts. Local gates do not establish deployed revision/health/auth/journey or Vercel administration acceptance; record those separately. New issue-specific regression journeys remain necessary where existing tests do not cover their failures.
e2e/README.md:35:Authenticated specs require `E2E_STORAGE_STATE` pointing at an ignored Playwright storage state, or `e2e/.auth.json`. Other gated specs create their own disposable users and require `SUPABASE_DB_URL`, the public Supabase variables and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. No production authentication bypass is used and no test emails are sent. Never commit credentials, auth state, private statements or detailed private evidence. A skipped required authenticated spec is not a pass.
e2e/README.md:46:- `pending-holds.gated.spec.ts` requires migration `202610060010`; it verifies atomic reviewed import settlement, changed amount/date, exact forecast release, partial settlement and undo with both original source observations retained. Missing prerequisites or migration fail explicitly. Run rollback-only fresh SQL first with `node supabase/tests/run-pending-holds.mjs`; that command does not deploy the migration or establish browser acceptance.
e2e/README.md:54:Final acceptance also requires unit tests (enable live DB resolver parity), lint/build, fresh/upgraded schema checks and deployed revision/health/auth/journey checks. Production Vercel administration/cron/logs require actual project access; local success does not establish deployment success.
supabase/tests/README.md:7:Run `node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs` with the existing `.env` configuration. The script verifies that `SUPABASE_DB_URL` targets `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, then tests pending migrations against the deployed application schema and replays every migration into a temporary isolated schema. It compares columns, constraints, indexes, RLS, policies, views, triggers and application functions, and runs the synthetic `.sql` regressions on both paths.
supabase/tests/README.md:21:Run `node supabase/tests/summary-live.mjs` with the local app running and its existing `CRON_SECRET` configured to verify actual cron dispatch, free-model review completion, period deduplication, cancellation and disabling. It uses a disposable empty workspace and targeted cleanup. This verifies the local endpoint/workflow; it does not prove that Vercel's external daily cron has been deployed.
supabase/tests/README.md:23:Run `npx playwright test e2e/two-user-isolation.gated.spec.ts --reporter=list` for two real disposable authenticated users. It exercises page/API/file ownership, denied foreign review cancellation, account editing/archive/sequential undo, saved view rename/removal/filter replacement/undo, Home insight dismissal/restore, exact large relevance thresholds and type mute/unmute. It requires the configured admin/auth/database environment, sends no email, uses no saved credentials or mocked backend, and removes its fixtures. Recovery IDs are written to ignored `.qa` files only if interrupted.
supabase/tests/README.md:31:Deployment is separate: `node supabase/tests/apply-migrations.mjs VERSION...` applies only explicitly listed ordered versions after review and rollback verification. It verifies the configured project, refuses skipped earlier pending files, locks migration history, compares names/content hashes, applies SQL and history atomically, and verifies hashes afterward. Do not run it as a routine test.
lib/scheduler.ts:1:// Self-hosted Moneo runs its background jobs from the server process instead of Vercel Cron.

content.text:
I've removed the code left over from the hosted version, in two more commits on `t3/self-hosted`. Unit tests, lint and the production build pass; the full browser test suite is running now against the production build, and I'll report its results when it finishes.

**What's gone from the app:**
- **Privacy and Terms pages.** They described a hosted service that no longer exists.
- **The Vercel-only startup branch, and the browser-side Supabase client**, which only the deleted sign-in pages used.
- **The `delete_account` database function**, dropped through a new migration, which I've applied to your local database. With one owner it has no use, and leaving it would let any signed-in session delete the owner. "Reset all data" is still in Settings.
- **The old sign-in page, now renamed `/setup`.** It only appears if the automatic sign-in fails, and tells you to run `npm run setup`.

**What changed in the tests:**
- Specs and SQL test scripts no longer insist the database is a hosted Supabase project or require SSL. That check was behind most of the failures in the earlier browser run.
- I deleted the browser tests for the removed sign-in, sign-out and account-deletion screens, and one spec that signed a test user in through the old login form now sets its session cookie directly.
- The test READMEs no longer mention Vercel deploys or crons.

**Checks:**
- Unit tests: 1,315 pass.
- One recurring-page test failed once during the full run but passed on its own, so I'll check whether it fails again.
- Lint is clean apart from one leftover unused-variable warning in a test file, which I'll fix with the browser-test results.
- `npm run build` passes.

Nothing has been pushed yet.

Most sources credit Forrest Chang, whose repo is forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills, though one source gives the author as Jiayuan Chang.

The four principles:

- **Think Before Coding:** Ask about unclear points rather than guessing, and present multiple interpretations instead of silently choosing one. It requires the agent to state assumptions, push back when simpler approaches exist, and stop when confused.
- **Simplicity First:** Aim for the least code that solves the problem, with no speculative features or single-use abstractions. A sanity check is whether a senior engineer would call the code overcomplicated.
- **Surgical Changes:** Edit only what the task requires. Remove only the imports or functions your own changes orphaned, and leave pre-existing dead code alone unless asked. If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it — don't delete it.
- **Goal-Driven Execution:** Turn vague instructions into verifiable goals, such as writing a test that reproduces a bug before fixing it. Strong success criteria let the LLM loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

The guidelines also note they bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks (simple typo fixes, obvious one-liners), use judgment.

I've summarized the document rather than reproducing it, since you asked for a concise response. It's a guidance file for agents working on T3 Code.

**What T3 Code is:** A minimal GUI for coding agents. A Node WebSocket server wraps provider CLIs (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Antigravity, Kiro) and serves web, desktop, and mobile clients.

**Non-negotiables:**
- **Open at the core:** Share the roadmap, reasoning, and code. Many users run forks.
- **Performance:** Avoid oversized websocket payloads, GPU-heavy CSS animations, and hard-to-render lists.
- **Remote ready:** New features must work over local network, Tailscale, and T3 Connect.
- **Multi-surface:** Support web (hosted and local `npx t3`), desktop (Electron, can host a server), and mobile (React Native).

**Philosophy (from Theo's note):** Prefer simple, minimal designs. Avoid scope creep and unnecessary machinery. These are defaults, and the developer's preferences override them.

**Safety rules for the agent:**
1. Never kill processes by name or pattern. Only kill PIDs you spawned or verified by port and working directory.
2. Never write to or start a server against the developer's live `~/.t3/userdata`. Copying from it is fine.
3. Never set `VITE_HTTP_URL` or `VITE_WS_URL` for dev. Dev uses a single origin with Vite proxying.

**Hit every surface:** Before calling frontend work done, check entry points, clients, providers, agents (MCP and scheduled tasks), contracts, reverse states (e.g., unsnooze, reopen), connection modes, and docs.

**Dev workflow:**
- Install with `vp i`, and wait for setup markers if setup is running.
- Start with `vp run dev`, and read real ports from the `[dev-runner]` line.
- Sharing uses `vp run dev --share`, then the `pairingUrl`. Don't wire up Tailscale manually or use the user's pairing link.
- Reuse dev auth across worktrees through a gitignored `T3CODE_DEV_AUTH_TOKEN`. Never commit it.
- Create second checkouts with `git worktree add` beside the current one, and remove them when done.

**Test data:** Seed the worktree's database from a copy of real data, using `vp run migrate-dev-db` with the dev server stopped. Copy, never symlink.

**Verification:**
- Run `vp run check:changed` before pushing. Don't run repo-wide checks unless asked.
- Test at the lowest layer that fails on `main`. Extend existing tables before adding new cases.
- Bug fixes need a failing test first, except purely visual bugs, which need before/after captures.
- Don't use sleeps, polling, or timeouts in tests. Await deterministic events instead.
- Use the free Replay provider for streaming tests. Real provider turns cost money.
- Mobile installs go through `vp run mobile:install`, not full native rebuilds.

**Evals:** Changes to model-facing text (instructions, tool descriptions, titles) should follow `evals/README.md`.

**Pull requests:**
- Never open a PR unless the developer explicitly asks.
- Use conventional commit titles and plain-language bodies.
- Include before/after images for UI changes and video for motion.
- One request per PR.
- When babysitting a PR, wait for notifications rather than polling, verify bot findings, and stop when checks are green.

**Documentation:** Most changes need no docs. Internal docs cover only decisions and cross-boundary constraints. User docs stay in the product's voice, and operations docs cover maintainer procedures.

**Plans:** Don't commit plans, research notes, or scratch files. Track work in GitHub issues.

**How it works:** Clients send typed WebSocket requests, which become commands. The orchestrator decides events without doing I/O. The event sink commits events, projections, and receipts in one transaction. The effect worker then runs side effects, such as provider turns and git checkpoints, and feeds results back as commands. Per-provider adapters translate native protocols.

**Code layout:** `apps/server` (Effect-heavy backend), `apps/web` (React/Vite), `apps/desktop`, `apps/mobile`, `apps/marketing`, and shared packages `contracts`, `shared`, and `client-runtime`. `.repos/` is read-only reference material.

**Taste:**
- Keep complexity at the adapter boundary. Orchestration stays pure, and the UI stays simple.
- Client mutations use `createEnvironmentRpcCommand`, and transports stay thin, delegating to services.
- Use `Effect.fn("Service.operation")` for reusable Effect functions.
- Prefer inferred types, and avoid `any`.
- Comments are rare and short, only for constraints the code can't express.
- React effects are only for syncing with external systems.
- No continuously repainting animations.
- If a rule conflicts with the task, flag it and get human sign-off.

**Security:** Matters, but don't over-index on it for dev-mode or maintainer-only features.

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source, self-hosted Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript personal-finance app. Its backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth/PostgREST/Storage services in Docker (`docker-compose.yml`, bound to 127.0.0.1), with Drizzle, Workflow (local world), Vitest/Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK (ChatGPT plan or API key; OpenRouter for vendor/model IDs). One owner is signed in automatically; there is no sign-in screen.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes .env secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev`
- Unit: `npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e`

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router UI, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — model/provider behavior
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows

## Rules
- Find the simplest cleanest way of doing something 
- Keep changes scoped; follow nearby patterns and prefer existing utilities/dependencies.
- Validate user/external input; Zod is the established pattern.
- Financial truth comes from application code/data, not AI guesses. Keep money in integer minor units/`bigint` and currencies explicit.
- Preserve source records, correction/history, and undo semantics when changing financial data flows.
- For schema changes, add a new ordered migration and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Do not rewrite applied migrations.
- Migrations are applied by `npm run setup` (history in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`). For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).
- for each thing break it down and for each thing make a commit directly if a big task make multiple commits

## Validation

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test` and `npm run lint`; add `npm run build` for app/config/build changes and Playwright for changed user flows. Gated E2E requires configured Supabase/auth; see `e2e/README.md`.

Signed-in E2E uses one persistent QA user, separate from the owner (login in the git-ignored `.env` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`). With the backend running:
   54 e2e/README.md
   31 supabase/tests/README.md
   36 BACKLOG.md
  121 total

questions.question: Moneo has no LICENSE file, which an open-source release needs. Which license should I add?

options.label: MIT (Recommended)
options.description: Simplest and most permissive: anyone can use, fork or sell it, as long as they keep your copyright notice. Most common for portfolio projects.

options.label: AGPL-3.0
options.description: Anyone who runs a modified Moneo as a service must publish their changes. Stops someone from turning it into a closed hosted product.

options.label: Apache-2.0
options.description: Permissive like MIT, plus an explicit patent grant. A bit more legal text.

options.label: No license for now
options.description: Leave it out; the code stays all-rights-reserved until you decide.

questions.question: How should the README read, given it's both your portfolio piece and the install guide?

options.label: Showcase + install (Recommended)
options.description: Short pitch, feature list (artifacts, voice calls, bank and Scalable sync, ChatGPT sign-in), a screenshot slot and the existing demo video, then setup. Detailed setup steps stay below.

options.label: Install guide only
options.description: Keep it minimal and practical, like now: what it is, how to run it, optional integrations.

questions.question: e2e/README.md and supabase/tests/README.md are dense acceptance-gate notes from the hosted era (migration IDs, ticket names, deploy gates). How far should I go?

options.label: Rewrite short (Recommended)
options.description: Replace each with a short, current guide: how to run unit, SQL and browser tests locally, what the QA user is, what each test tier covers. Drop the old acceptance-gate essays.

options.label: Light edit only
options.description: Keep the existing text and only fix what's wrong for self-hosting.

questions.question: Which of these T3 Code-style sections should AGENTS.md have? (Karpathy's four principles go in either way: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes, goal-driven verification.)

options.label: Non-negotiables
options.description: Moneo's product rules: local-first on 127.0.0.1, one owner, financial truth from code, minor units, history/undo, open source.

options.label: Safety rules
options.description: Never touch the owner's real workspace in tests (use the QA user), never `docker compose down -v`, only kill PIDs you started, never commit .env/.data.

options.label: Hit every surface
options.description: Before calling a feature done, check pages, chat tools, voice call, Home widgets, scheduled jobs, undo paths and docs.

options.label: Commits and PRs
options.description: One commit per step (your rule), never open a PR unless asked, plain-language messages, no scratch files or plans committed.

4	Open Moneo on your phone from any network, like T3 Code, with nothing to install on the phone. Moneo only listens on 127.0.0.1 today, and it signs its owner in automatically, so any remote access must add a login first (an `APP_PASSWORD` sign-in, or Cloudflare Access).
5	- Options weighed: Tailscale Funnel (free, fixed `*.ts.net` URL, nothing on the phone), Cloudflare Tunnel (free tunnel; a fixed URL needs your own domain, about $10/yr), or Tailscale with its phone app (private, no password needed).
6	- HTTPS is required for voice: browsers only give web pages the microphone over a secure connection.
7	- Callbacks: ChatGPT sign-in only accepts a 127.0.0.1 callback and Scalable's login accepts localhost freely, so both are connected from the computer Moneo runs on; their syncs then work from anywhere.
8	
9	## Self-hosted: real banks need an HTTPS callback
10	Enable Banking production apps accept only `https://` redirect URLs, and Moneo runs on `http://localhost`. Sandbox apps (mock banks) work today. Options: a static HTTPS page (for example on GitHub Pages) that forwards `code` and `state` to `http://localhost:3000/api/bank/callback` in the owner's own browser, or serving Moneo on `https://localhost` if Enable Banking accepts it. The phone-access tunnel above would also provide an HTTPS address.
11	
12	
13	## Multi-currency on Home
14	Home is built for one currency (the workspace display currency) for now.
15	- Recorded net worth by currency: Home used to list each currency's recorded total and the observations behind it (removed with the redesign; the Wealth page still shows net worth per currency).
16	- Net worth chart: plots only display-currency balances and valuations; convert others with the rate dated on or before each month end.
17	- Cash flow (month card and six-month chart): no "partial" marker when rows lack a rate; surface it again once FX is handled.
18	- Budgets and Coming up: amounts in other currencies are left out.

# Database regression checks

Run `node supabase/tests/run-recurring-occurrences.mjs` for migration `202610060003` and its explicit occurrence fixture on the configured database. It checks current-owner/version/date guards, partial/full and pending-to-posted receipts, undo/reassociation/deletion history and authenticated isolation. Candidate schema and migration history are verified unchanged after rollback.

Run `node supabase/tests/recurring-occurrence-concurrency.mjs` to check association versus transaction correction on separate authenticated connections. It creates only a disposable application schema with synthetic users, verifies correction/association lock order and stale-version rejection, then drops that exact schema and verifies cleanup. Public migration history and schema privileges remain unchanged; an ignored `.qa` recovery journal records the disposable schema if interrupted.

Run `node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs` with the existing `.env` configuration. The script tests pending migrations against the current application schema and replays every migration into a temporary isolated schema. It compares columns, constraints, indexes, RLS, policies, views, triggers and application functions, and runs the synthetic `.sql` regressions on both paths.

All writes run inside rollback-only transactions. Migration history stays unchanged, and the script verifies that its temporary schema was removed. It does not apply migrations permanently. Fresh verification uses an empty `auth.users` surrogate and skips Supabase-owned storage bucket/policy setup; full Supabase platform bootstrap still requires a disposable local Supabase instance.

`workspace-isolation.sql` seeds two synthetic users and foreign records in every current application table. It switches to the actual `authenticated` database role to check row visibility and foreign-target RPC denial. Keep its fixture list and RPC cases aligned when adding tables or mutations.

Run `node supabase/tests/precision.mjs` to verify the actual Money/budget page SELECTs through PostgREST with amounts beyond JavaScript's safe integer range. This check temporarily commits a synthetic user/workspace and removes only those records in `finally`; it verifies cleanup. It requires the existing service-role key, which is never printed.

Run `node supabase/tests/chat-concurrency.mjs` after migration 023 is applied to check duplicate claims and cancellation on separate authenticated connections. It verifies cancellation waits for the execution lock and prevents later corrections/replies, then removes its synthetic user/workspace.

Run `node supabase/tests/review-concurrency.mjs` after migration 043 is applied to exercise review finish/cancel and first preference-insert races on separate real authenticated/service connections. Cancellation or scope revocation prevents analysis persistence; a committed finisher retains its historical result. Synthetic fixtures are removed by exact IDs.

Run `node supabase/tests/import-concurrency.mjs` after migration 051 is applied to check cancellation and ingestion on separate authenticated/service connections. It observes the specific waiter and holder database process locks, verifies cancellation cannot admit later row effects, retains already committed source evidence, fences old workers after resume and deduplicates simultaneous retries. Its exact large-money synthetic records are removed by ID.

Run `node supabase/tests/summary-live.mjs` with the local app running and its existing `CRON_SECRET` configured to verify actual cron dispatch, free-model review completion, period deduplication, cancellation and disabling. It uses a disposable empty workspace and targeted cleanup. The running server's scheduler calls the same endpoint hourly.

Run `npx playwright test e2e/two-user-isolation.gated.spec.ts --reporter=list` for two real disposable authenticated users. It exercises page/API/file ownership, denied foreign review cancellation, account editing/archive/sequential undo, saved view rename/removal/filter replacement/undo, Home insight dismissal/restore, exact large relevance thresholds and type mute/unmute. It requires the configured admin/auth/database environment, sends no email, uses no saved credentials or mocked backend, and removes its fixtures. Recovery IDs are written to ignored `.qa` files only if interrupted.

`insight-preferences.sql` checks owner isolation, exact thresholds beyond JavaScript's safe integer range, dismissal deduplication, bounded lookahead and dismissal restoration. The pure insight fixtures cover all nine supported types, dated evidence changes, ambiguity suppression, half-up medians and filling the item limit after dismissed evidence is removed. Insights make no model calls.

For the targeted import review regression only, use `node supabase/tests/run-sql.mjs --candidate` before applying migration 020, or omit `--candidate` afterward. It also rolls back its synthetic fixtures and candidate function replacement.

Run `node supabase/tests/run-goal-reservations.mjs` for the reservation boundary/history fixture. For SQL/application resolver parity, run `RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS=1 npm test -- lib/finance/reservation-balance.live.test.ts` (PowerShell: set `$env:RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS='1'` first). This opt-in test compares six synthetic balance fixtures and rolls everything back.

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services in Docker (`docker-compose.yml`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`. Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Anything that exposes Moneo beyond this computer must add a login first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts with a test that fails on the current code. Purely visual changes get a before/after screenshot instead.

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's workspace. Browser tests use the QA user (`scripts/e2e-auth.mjs`) or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop the database: that is the owner's financial history.
- Never change `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`; keys, sessions and stored bank and ChatGPT tokens stop working.
- Never commit `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `.data/`, `e2e/.auth.json` or `.qa/`.
- Only kill processes you started, or ones you verified by port and working directory. Never kill by name.
- Real AI, bank and Scalable calls cost money or count against limits (PSD2 allows about 4 background bank fetches a day). Mock them in tests unless the task is to check the real service.

## Hit every surface

Before calling a feature done, check where else it shows up:

- Pages and their mobile layout, light and dark.
- Chat tools and the system prompt in `lib/ai/provider.ts`, artifacts, and the voice call (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Home widgets and the command palette.
- Background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `workflows/`) and imports from files, banks and Scalable.
- The reverse path: undo, reset all data, reconnect, disconnect.
- Docs: `README.md` for anything the owner sets up or runs, `.env.example` for new variables, `BACKLOG.md` for deferred work.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes `.env` secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev` (http://localhost:3000)
- Unit: `npm test` · Lint: `npm run lint` · Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router pages, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — models, chat tools, ChatGPT sign-in (`chatgpt.ts`), voice
- `lib/bank/`, `lib/scalable/` — Enable Banking and Scalable Capital
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs; `lib/scheduler.ts` runs the daily ones
- `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/`, `scripts/setup.mjs` — the self-hosted backend
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows; `supabase/tests/` — SQL regressions

## Database changes

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/` and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Validation

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test` and `npm run lint`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. Await real events in tests; don't add sleeps or polling.

## Commits and pull requests

- Break the work into steps and commit each one; a big task is several commits.
- Never open a pull request unless asked.
- Write commit messages in plain language: what changed and why.
- Don't commit plans, research notes or scratch files. Deferred work goes in `BACKLOG.md`.

## Context

Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, `e2e/README.md` for browser tests, `supabase/tests/README.md` for SQL checks.

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source, self-hosted Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript personal-finance app. Its backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth/PostgREST/Storage services in Docker (`docker-compose.yml`, bound to 127.0.0.1), with Drizzle, Workflow (local world), Vitest/Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK (ChatGPT plan or API key; OpenRouter for vendor/model IDs). One owner is signed in automatically; there is no sign-in screen.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes .env secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev`
- Unit: `npm test`
- Lint: `npm run lint`
- Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e`

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router UI, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — model/provider behavior
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows

## Rules
- Find the simplest cleanest way of doing something 
- Keep changes scoped; follow nearby patterns and prefer existing utilities/dependencies.
- Validate user/external input; Zod is the established pattern.
- Financial truth comes from application code/data, not AI guesses. Keep money in integer minor units/`bigint` and currencies explicit.
- Preserve source records, correction/history, and undo semantics when changing financial data flows.

# Browser tests

Playwright tests run against the app on http://localhost:3000. The config starts it (`npm run dev`, or the production build with `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`) unless a server is already running there.

## Setup

1. Start the backend: `npm run setup`.
2. Create the QA user and save its session: `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs`. Its login is stored in `.env` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, and its session in `e2e/.auth.json` (or set `E2E_STORAGE_STATE`).
3. Before a full run, empty its workspace: `node --env-file=.env scripts/e2e-auth.mjs --reset`. Never delete the user.

Tests never use the owner's workspace: a saved QA session takes the place of the owner's automatic sign-in.

## Running

```sh
npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1
```

Use one worker: several specs change the same QA workspace and its preferences. Stop a running server on port 3000 before `npm run build`, so the two don't write `.next` at the same time.

## Kinds of specs

- `*.smoke.spec.ts` and `*.mocked.spec.ts` need no saved session; mocked specs stub API responses to check UI contracts.
- `*.gated.spec.ts` need the backend. Most use the QA session; others create disposable users with the service key, sign them in by session cookie, and remove them in `finally`. If interrupted, their IDs are left in ignored `.qa/` files for cleanup.
- `core-journey.gated.spec.ts` calls the real AI provider, so it costs money: run it only when you mean to.
- `review-runtime.config.ts` and `review-investigation.config.ts` run the real Workflow engine against local synthetic database and model servers (ports 3040/3041), including a server restart mid-review: `npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts`.

A skipped spec is not a pass: it means a prerequisite (backend, QA session, service key) is missing.

## Acceptance

`npm run acceptance:fast` runs unit tests, lint and the build. `npm run acceptance:required` then runs the SQL regressions, live database checks and the browser suite on that build with one worker. Results go to an ignored `.qa/acceptance-*` folder; logs there may contain workspace data, so keep them out of the repo.

# Database checks

These scripts test the SQL functions, row-level security and concurrency of the self-hosted database. They read `SUPABASE_DB_URL` and the Supabase keys from `.env` (written by `npm run setup`).

## Migrations and regressions

```sh
node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs
```

Replays every migration into a temporary schema, compares it with the current schema (columns, constraints, indexes, RLS, policies, views, triggers, functions), and runs the `.sql` regression fixtures on both. Everything runs in rollback-only transactions; migration history stays unchanged and the temporary schema is removed.

`workspace-isolation.sql` seeds two synthetic users with records in every application table and checks, as the `authenticated` role, that neither can see or change the other's data. Keep its fixtures and RPC cases in step when adding tables or mutations.

Single regressions run with their `run-*.mjs` script, for example `node supabase/tests/run-goal-reservations.mjs`. `run-sql.mjs` runs the import-review fixture.

## Concurrency

`*-concurrency.mjs` scripts (chat, imports, reviews, recurring occurrences, reservations) open separate authenticated and service connections to check locks, cancellation and duplicate claims. They create synthetic users or a disposable schema, remove them by exact ID, and leave a recovery note in ignored `.qa/` files if interrupted.

## Live checks

- `precision.mjs` reads Money and budget pages through PostgREST with amounts beyond JavaScript's safe integer range.
- `summary-live.mjs` (with the app running) checks scheduled summaries end to end: dispatch, deduplication per period, cancellation and disabling.
- Opt-in unit tests compare SQL with application logic, for example `RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS=1 npm test -- lib/finance/reservation-balance.live.test.ts` (PowerShell: `$env:RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS='1'` first).

None of these touch the owner's workspace. Migrations themselves are applied by `npm run setup`.

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services in Docker (`docker-compose.yml`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`. Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Anything that exposes Moneo beyond this computer must add a login first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts with a test that fails on the current code. Purely visual changes get a before/after screenshot instead.

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's workspace. Browser tests use the QA user (`scripts/e2e-auth.mjs`) or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop the database: that is the owner's financial history.
- Never change `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`; keys, sessions and stored bank and ChatGPT tokens stop working.
- Never commit `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `.data/`, `e2e/.auth.json` or `.qa/`.
- Only kill processes you started, or ones you verified by port and working directory. Never kill by name.
- Real AI, bank and Scalable calls cost money or count against limits (PSD2 allows about 4 background bank fetches a day). Mock them in tests unless the task is to check the real service.

## Hit every surface

Before calling a feature done, check where else it shows up:

- Pages and their mobile layout, light and dark.
- Chat tools and the system prompt in `lib/ai/provider.ts`, artifacts, and the voice call (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Home widgets and the command palette.
- Background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `workflows/`) and imports from files, banks and Scalable.
- The reverse path: undo, reset all data, reconnect, disconnect.
- Docs: `README.md` for anything the owner sets up or runs, `.env.example` for new variables, `BACKLOG.md` for deferred work.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes `.env` secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev` (http://localhost:3000)
- Unit: `npm test` · Lint: `npm run lint` · Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router pages, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — models, chat tools, ChatGPT sign-in (`chatgpt.ts`), voice
- `lib/bank/`, `lib/scalable/` — Enable Banking and Scalable Capital
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs; `lib/scheduler.ts` runs the daily ones
- `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/`, `scripts/setup.mjs` — the self-hosted backend
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows; `supabase/tests/` — SQL regressions

## Database changes

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/` and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Validation

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test` and `npm run lint`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. Await real events in tests; don't add sleeps or polling.

## Commits and pull requests

- Break the work into steps and commit each one; a big task is several commits.
- Never open a pull request unless asked.
- Write commit messages in plain language: what changed and why.
- Don't commit plans, research notes or scratch files. Deferred work goes in `BACKLOG.md`.

## Context

Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, `e2e/README.md` for browser tests, `supabase/tests/README.md` for SQL checks.

lines:
No live browser maths on Home

A slider on a card asks the server to re-render, which is fast but not 60 fps. The Page (sandboxed iframe) keeps full client-side interactivity.

-

Durability equals chat's

A deploy or crash mid-build loses that run. The request shows as failed, and you ask again.

+

Durability equals chat's

A restart or crash mid-build loses that run. The request shows as failed, and you ask again.

A card can show a wrong number

The sandbox stops capabilities, not wrong arithmetic or labels: a card can compute or hard-code an amount and nothing rejects it. The preview, drafts and version history are how you catch and undo that. Enforcing it would mean cards bind to values instead of rendering them, which would cost the design freedom this version was built for.

Tailwind classes

Only classes the app already uses exist, so designed cards style themselves with style objects and scoped CSS.

content.text:
I've updated the docs and committed them on `t3/self-hosted`.

**AGENTS.md** is rewritten in the shape of T3 Code's AGENTS.md, with the four Karpathy-style principles for how to work:
- **Non-negotiables:**
  - Everything runs on `127.0.0.1`, with one owner and no accounts.
  - Financial figures come from code and data, with money kept in minor units.
  - The AI only proposes changes the owner accepts.
  - History and undo are kept, and no secrets or personal data go in the repo.
- **How to work:** think before coding, keep it simple, change only what the task needs, and turn each task into checks that can pass or fail.
- **Safety:** never test against the owner's workspace or delete the Docker volumes, never change the secrets in an existing `.env`, only kill processes you started, never commit `.env`, `.data/` or test sessions, and mock paid or rate-limited services in tests.
- **Hit every surface:** before calling a feature done, check pages, chat tools, voice, Home widgets, background jobs, undo paths and docs.
- **Commits and PRs:** one commit per step, no PR unless you ask, and no plans or scratch files committed.
- I kept the commands, project map and database rules. The block that `next dev` writes at the end is unchanged, since it re-adds it anyway.

**Other docs:**
- **`LICENSE`:** MIT, copyright "indkhan". Let me know if you want your full name there instead.
- **`README.md`:** stays an install guide, as you chose, now with a license line.
- **`e2e/README.md` and `supabase/tests/README.md`:** short, current guides covering setup, how to run each kind of test, and what each one checks. They replace the old hosted-era notes about deploy checks and migration IDs.
- **Small leftovers:** a "deploy" mention in `docs/artifact-cards-architecture.html` and the environment label the acceptance script writes now refer to the local setup.

The full browser test run is still going (test 47 of 82). I'll send you the results when it finishes.

Sources:
- [T3 Code AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/main/AGENTS.md)
